components.name: Reading Capsule
components.description: Rounded capsule for every live on-screen number (the overlay's readings and a pin's zoom, opacity, Copied, and Locked), with optional color swatch. A color pin's hex is the one resting value: it shows while no other reading does and a passing reading gives way back to it at once. Nothing in it animates on its own: geometry, text, and colors change at once, so no number trails the pointer; a surface that fades it animates only its opacity. Light shown; Dark uses rgba(43,43,46,0.94) fill and 0.92 white ink.

components.name: Pin
components.description: A picture kept above every app's windows (the Text Pin and Color Pin below share this window, its controls, reading, ring, and lock mark): a borderless, non-activating floating panel on every Space and over full-screen apps that takes the keys only when clicked. Continuous corners from Settings (0-24 pt, 12 default), the system window shadow, a 0.5 pt black 0.18 hairline (1 pt black 0.35 under Increase Contrast), and a 1.5 pt keyboardFocusIndicatorColor ring inside the edge while key. On hover (unlocked) Close and More card corner buttons fade in 8 pt from the top corners, centered in the height of a pin under 40 pt tall; Close needs at least 40 x 36 pt and More at least 72 pt of width, and faded out they take no clicks; a reading capsule 10 pt above the bottom shows zoom, opacity, Copied, or Locked for 0.9 s, then fades over 0.12 s. Scroll or pinch zooms around the pointer (10-800%), Option-scroll fades the picture only (20-100%). A locked pin lets clicks through and wears a lock.fill disc where More would be.

components.name: Text Pin
components.description: The clipboard's text kept above every app's windows, in the Pin's window: a card in the Text Result Card's materials (capsule surface white 0.97, Dark a 0.17 gray at 0.96; the reading capsule's 0.5 pt black 0.08 / white 0.12 hairline from Settings › Edge, 1 pt black 0.35 / white 0.5 and always shown under Increase Contrast), with the Pin's Settings corners, window shadow, and ring. Label ink, 14 x 11 pt padding, the system face at 13 pt, or monospaced at 12 pt for code (a fenced block, or two or more indented lines). As wide as its text, 64 to 420 pt; cut at 30 lines with an ellipsis and never more than 4000 characters laid out, while Copy Text (⌘C) takes everything. Laid out once at 100% and drawn scaled with the zoom, so it wraps alike at every zoom. The text takes no clicks; the whole card drags. Its Close and More stand on the card's own fill, so on a one-line card, where they center over the line's ends, they hide the letters they cover instead of showing them through the disc. VoiceOver: static text, "Text pin: " and its text, actions Copy, Lock, Close. No Save, Annotate, or Recognize Text. Light shown; Dark uses rgba(43,43,46,0.96) fill, white 0.12 hairline, and white label ink.
components.html: Pinned notes stay above every window. The text wraps the same at any zoom. Copy Text takes all of it.

components.name: Color Pin
components.description: A copied color (or text that is exactly #RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, rgb(), or rgba()) kept above every app's windows, in the Pin's window: a 128 x 128 pt swatch in the color's own color space, with the Pin's Settings corners, window shadow, 0.5 pt black 0.18 hairline, and ring. A translucent color sits over the checkerboard token, 8 pt squares on screen at every zoom (white and 0.91 gray; Dark 0.20 and 0.25; 0.84 and 0.30 under Increase Contrast). Its hex ("#3366FF", "#3366FF80" when translucent) rests in the reading capsule while the swatch is at least the capsule plus 16 pt in width and height, and hides otherwise; zoom, opacity, and Copied pass and give way back to it instead of fading. Menu: Copy Hex (⌘C) and Copy RGB (rgb() or rgba()), then Zoom, Opacity, Lock, Close, Close All Pins. Opacity fades the swatch and checkerboard only. VoiceOver: an image, "Color pin, #3366FF", actions Copy Hex, Copy RGB, Lock, Close.

components.name: In-Place Toolbar
components.description: Annotate Area's toolbar beside the selection over the frozen screen: the tool rail laid flat, a 42 pt Liquid Glass capsule (opaque window-colored backing, 0.5 pt separator hairline, floating bar shadow) of 30 pt circular chips 6 pt inside, groups split by 18 pt separators: drawing tools | Text, Counter | Redact, Spotlight | Undo, Redo | Open in Editor, Save, Cancel, Copy (checkmark in the accent). No Select chip; the tool in hand takes the selected fill and accent symbol. Stands 10 pt below the selection, right-aligned, with the style capsule 6 pt under it; above, or inside the bottom-right, when there is no room. Approximated with an opaque fill; Reduce Transparency is a solid capsule.
components.css: .ds-ipt{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:2px;height:42px;padding:6px;box-sizing:border-box;border-radius:9999px;background:#FFFFFF;border:0.5px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.1);box-shadow:0 3px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.16);} .ds-ipt-chip{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:30px;height:30px;padding:0;border:none;border-radius:9999px;background:transparent;color:rgba(0,0,0,0.85);cursor:default;} .ds-ipt-chip:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.045);} .ds-ipt-chip:disabled{color:rgba(0,0,0,0.26);background:transparent;} .ds-ipt-chip:focus-visible{outline:2px solid AccentColor;outline-offset:1px;} .ds-ipt-on,.ds-ipt-on:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.08);color:AccentColor;} .ds-ipt-copy{color:AccentColor;} .ds-ipt-sep{width:1px;height:18px;margin:0 4px;background:rgba(0,0,0,0.1);} @media (prefers-contrast: more){.ds-ipt{border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.35);} .ds-ipt-on{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.16);} .ds-ipt-chip:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.09);}}

components.name: Self-Timer Countdown
components.description: Between choosing and capturing: the chosen area outlined as the capture overlay draws a selection (white 1.5 pt edge over the 0.32 dark outline, no dimming), one click-through panel per display, and a 64 pt disc centered 12 pt below it (above it, else inside its bottom edge; 8 pt from display edges). The disc is Liquid Glass over an opaque window-colored backing (solid under Reduce Transparency) with the seconds left in the reading face at 26 pt and a 2.5 pt accent ring inset 6 pt running out over a label-ink 0.12 track (0.3 under Increase Contrast); 0.5 pt separator rim (1 pt contrast hairline under Increase Contrast); floating bar shadow. Panels sit just above pop-up menus, never activate the app, and are left out of the capture, which is taken live at zero. Approximated with an opaque fill.

components.css: .ds-timer{position:relative;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:64px;height:64px;border-radius:9999px;background:#FFFFFF;border:0.5px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.1);box-sizing:border-box;box-shadow:0 3px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.16);} .ds-timer-ring{position:absolute;inset:-0.5px;} .ds-timer-digit{position:relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Rounded', ui-rounded, system-ui, sans-serif;font-size:26px;font-weight:600;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:rgba(0,0,0,0.85);} @media (prefers-contrast: more){.ds-timer{border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.35);} .ds-timer-ring circle:first-child{stroke:rgba(0,0,0,0.3);}}

components.name: Tool Rail
components.description: The editor's tools: a 42 pt Liquid Glass capsule (opaque window-colored backing, 0.5 pt separator hairline, floating bar shadow) of 30 pt circular chips in groups split by 18 pt hairlines; the last group is Crop and Background (G). Tool in hand: selected chip fill and accent symbol. Approximated with an opaque fill; Reduce Transparency is a solid capsule.
components.css: .ds-rail{display:inline-flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:2px;width:42px;padding:6px;box-sizing:border-box;border-radius:9999px;background:#FFFFFF;border:0.5px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.1);box-shadow:0 3px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.16);} .ds-rail-chip{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:30px;height:30px;padding:0;border:none;border-radius:9999px;background:transparent;color:rgba(0,0,0,0.85);cursor:default;} .ds-rail-chip:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.045);} .ds-rail-chip:focus-visible{outline:2px solid AccentColor;outline-offset:1px;} .ds-rail-on,.ds-rail-on:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.08);color:AccentColor;} .ds-rail-sep{width:18px;height:1px;margin:4px 0;background:rgba(0,0,0,0.1);} @media (prefers-contrast: more){.ds-rail{border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.35);} .ds-rail-on{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.16);} .ds-rail-chip:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.09);}}

components.name: Style Capsule
components.description: A mark's style beside the mark: white 0.97 capsule, 38 pt tall, 0.5 pt hairline, floating reading shadow, no glass. Color dots (chosen one ringed in the accent), size dots, variants, Shadow, Delete, split by hairlines. Light shown; Dark uses a 0.17 gray at 0.96 and white 0.12 hairline. With the Background tool it holds 14 pt fill swatches in 24 pt chips (No Background, Transparent, ten gradients, Blurred Capture, Background Color…, Picture; the one in use ringed in the accent), then Adjust (a 320 pt grouped Form in the system popover) and Presets chips. A combined image shows only Shadow and Delete.
components.css: .ds-style{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:2px;height:38px;padding:4px 4px 4px 8px;box-sizing:border-box;border-radius:9999px;background:rgba(255,255,255,0.97);border:0.5px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.08);box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.18);color:rgba(0,0,0,0.85);} .ds-dot{width:24px;height:30px;padding:0;border:none;background:transparent;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;cursor:default;} .ds-dot::before{content:'';width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--c);box-shadow:0 0 0 0.5px rgba(0,0,0,0.18);} .ds-dot-on::before{box-shadow:0 0 0 0.5px rgba(0,0,0,0.18),0 0 0 2.5px #fff,0 0 0 4.5px AccentColor;} .ds-cchip{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:30px;height:30px;padding:0;border:none;border-radius:9999px;background:transparent;color:inherit;cursor:default;} .ds-size{width:26px;} .ds-size i{display:block;border-radius:50%;background:currentColor;} .ds-cchip:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.045);} .ds-cchip-on,.ds-cchip-on:hover{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.08);color:AccentColor;} .ds-cchip:focus-visible,.ds-dot:focus-visible{outline:2px solid AccentColor;outline-offset:1px;border-radius:9999px;} .ds-style-sep{width:1px;height:18px;margin:0 4px;background:rgba(0,0,0,0.1);} @media (prefers-contrast: more){.ds-style{border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.35);} .ds-cchip-on{background:rgba(0,0,0,0.16);}}

narrative.northStar: The Part of macOS Apple Forgot to Ship
narrative.overview:
OhMyShot looks like a system feature, not an app with a brand. Light and dark follow the system, the accent is the user's own macOS accent, and every window is a standard window with standard controls. What the app adds is a thin, consistent layer of softness for the things that float over other people's screens: continuous-corner cards, fully round capsules, gentle downward shadows, opaque white action capsules, and the rounded system face with fixed-width digits for every live reading. The capture is the hero; the chrome recedes.

Density is low and the vocabulary is small. A handful of shapes (12 pt cards, capsules, one circular loupe) and a handful of tints (black and white at stated opacities over system colors) cover every shipped surface: the capture overlay, the All-In-One bar, in-place annotation, the Self-Timer countdown, Quick Access cards, Capture History, the OCR panel, the annotation editor, and Settings. Light and dark are first-class and are resolved per view, and Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency, and Increase Contrast each have a shipped, specific response rather than a generic fallback.

The confirmed rejection is the first world, "Contact Sheet" (rejected by the user on 2026-10-07): no frame numbers, no captures joined into one strip, no film-edge or darkroom motifs, no dark heavy panels, nothing that reads as a Linux utility.

Units: every dimension in this file is in points. The frontmatter writes points as `px` for tool compatibility; 1 pt renders as 2 device pixels on Retina displays.
keyCharacteristics: System semantic colors and the user's accent carry all appearance; literal values are only black or white at fixed opacities.
Continuous corners everywhere: 12 pt cards, fully round capsules for every control and reading.
Soft, downward, widely blurred shadows; never a hard edge or a halo.
SF Pro Rounded with monospaced digits for readings; plain system text styles inside windows.
Liquid Glass only on small controls (the All-In-One bar, the in-place toolbar, the editor's tool rail, the Self-Timer disc, History hover buttons, window toolbars), never over a full-screen frame.
Motion is a single short ease-out or nothing; under Reduce Motion it is nothing.

rules.name: The No Brand Hue Rule
rules.body: The accent is whatever the user chose in System Settings. Never hard-code a blue in chrome, never tint a surface toward a house color. Mark inks and background fills are the user's content and the one place fixed hues live.

rules.name: The Black-and-White Opacity Rule
rules.body: Every literal color the app's chrome introduces is pure black or white at a stated opacity (or the single 0.17 gray of the Dark reading capsule, and the opaque grays of the on-screen checkerboard). New surfaces reuse these steps before inventing a tint.

rules.name: The Resolve-Per-Appearance Rule
rules.body: Layer colors do not follow appearance changes on their own; every layer-drawn color is resolved for the view's effective appearance and re-resolved when it changes.

rules.name: The Rounded-Off-Window Rule
rules.body: The rounded face is for floating controls and readings over the screen. Inside a standard window, use system text styles and never the rounded face. A counter's rounded numerals are content drawn into the picture, not chrome.

rules.name: The Steady Digits Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes while the user watches uses monospaced digits.

rules.name: The Soft Lift Rule
rules.body: Shadows are downward, widely blurred, and low opacity. No hard offset shadows, no glows, no halos.

rules.name: The Small Glass Rule
rules.body: Liquid Glass appears only on small controls: the All-In-One bar, the in-place toolbar, the editor's tool rail, the Self-Timer disc, window toolbars and their glassProminent Copy, and History hover buttons. The two overlay toolbars are small controls on the overlay, not over it; the full-screen overlay itself is a flat dimming fill and never carries glass, and neither does the editor's style capsule, which sits beside text-bearing marks.

rules.name: The Opaque Behind Text Rule
rules.body: Any control with text that floats over a capture or a screen has an opaque (or at least 0.94) fill. Glass supplies the rim, not the backing; the editor's Adjust popover sets its Form on the opaque window color inside the system popover.

rules.name: The Exported-Is-Drawn Rule
rules.body: What is drawn into the picture is exported: marks, the mark shadow, the background, its card shadow, and the matte. What helps on screen never is: the checkerboard, selection and handles, the drop ring, the crop frame and the in-place selection frame, the picture border, and the in-window shadow.

dos: **Do** use system semantic colors and `controlAccentColor` for every surface and state; add only black or white at the stated opacities.

**Do** make every floating control a full capsule (radius = height / 2) with concentric inner chips, and every picture a 12 pt continuous-corner card; the exceptions are a picture being edited for export, which shows its own square edges, and a pin, whose corners are the user's (0 to 24 pt, 12 by default).
**Do** give floating elements a soft downward shadow plus a 0.5 pt hairline so they hold on white pages.
**Do** put live numbers in a reading capsule: SF Pro Rounded 12 pt semibold with monospaced digits.
**Do** keep text-bearing controls opaque over captures; use glass for the rim, not the fill.

**Do** answer accessibility settings specifically: Reduce Motion = instant; Reduce Transparency = solid window-colored capsule; Increase Contrast = 45% dimming, 0.7 outline, 1 pt contrast hairlines and button outlines, doubled chip fills.
**Do** use standard windows, toolbars, grouped Forms, and SwiftUI glass button styles inside windows.

**Do** build chips in floating controls (the All-In-One bar, the in-place toolbar, the tool rail, the style capsule) as borderless buttons with the chip fills, and hand-draw whole controls only where AppKit would render them dimmed (non-key floating panels), tracking presses like standard buttons.
donts: **Don't** bring back Contact Sheet: no frame numbers, no captures joined into a strip, no film-edge or darkroom motifs.
**Don't** build dark heavy panels, bars, or strips; small dark round corner buttons over a hovered picture or pin, and a locked pin's mark in the same style, are the only dark chrome.
**Don't** put glass, blur, or a material over the full-screen overlay; the room is a flat 26% fill.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows, glows, or halos.
**Don't** use the rounded face inside standard windows, or proportional digits in a changing number.
**Don't** invent a brand hue or tint chrome toward one; fixed hues belong to mark inks only.
**Don't** animate anything that follows the pointer, or run any motion under Reduce Motion.
**Don't** give the editor a wide tool toolbar or a fixed option strip; tools live in the rail and a mark's style beside the mark.
